claims.claim: chr_b.bin's parsed data array is cached at a fixed offset (+0x40) inside a single global 'battle resource manager' singleton in RAM (literal 0x0214BD80, loaded via PC-relative pool at 0x020763BC/0x020763C0/etc.). The loader (arm9, part of the ~1KB battle-init routine starting 0x02075FBC) loads the chr_b.bin file handle, stores it into manager+0xc, re-derives handle->+4->vtable->[+0x2c] (a generic resource 'GetData' virtual call) and stores the RETURNED pointer -- the actual per-character record array -- into manager+0x40. The same generic sequence (open file, store handle, call vtable+0x2c, store result) repeats for every other combat .bin file (koma->manager+0x30, an unidentified 212-byte/record table->manager+0x44, a 20-byte/record 'combat stat' table->manager+0x48, a 12-byte/record table->manager+0x54, ...), all sharing this one manager struct, confirming +0x40 specifically is chr_b's slot (it is the load immediately preceded by the literal for the filename string 'bin/chr_b.bin' at 0x0209F5D4, independently confirmed via `query.py strings arm9`).

ANSWERS Q1 (chr_b record stride + statC offset). arm9 0x020771A0-0x020771C4 (inside the function at 0x02077178) computes a chr_b record pointer as manager(0x0214BD80)->field_0x40 + charIndex*0x3C (charIndex read from a character-context struct's own cached byte at offset +0x41, via 'ldrb r6,[r1,#0x41]'; 0x3C=60 matches the known chr_b.bin on-disk entry size, EntrySize=60 in src/JUS.Tool/Combat/Formats/BattleCharacterEntry.cs), then reads THREE consecutive 16-bit fields off that record base: +8 -> r6, +0xa -> r5, +0xc -> r3. These three offsets are EXACTLY statA(offset 8), statB(offset 10) and statC(offset 12) in the on-disk/converter layout (Binary2BattleCharacter.cs: FormType/Tier/KomaSize/CharId=0-3, Flags(u32)=4-7, StatA(u16)=8, StatB(u16)=10, StatC(u16)=12). This is the first and (per exhaustive cross-check in the next claim) only place in the whole ROM where chr_b's raw statC is read straight off the main per-character array via this base+60*index addressing -- i.e. RAM in-memory statC offset = +0xC within a 0x3C-byte record, base = *(0x0214BD80)+0x40, index = charStruct[+0x41].
open_questions: This same 0x0214BD80/+0x41-indexed pointer chain is reused across the ROM (arm9 loader + ~44 ov5 sites + 1 ov6 + 1 ov11), but ONLY this one site (0x020771C4) and the sibling clean getter cited below (record offset +0) actually dereference the +0x40 chr_b array with the #0x3c stride; none of the others reach offset +0xC. That means the walk-speed tier selector, if it exists as a classic cmp-chain, is NOT among the ~50 code sites that load the literal 0x0214BD80 -- it must consume a value cached elsewhere (see suggested_next_angles).

claims.claim: Sibling confirmation of the base+stride mechanism from claim 2 (record offset +0 = FormType, matching FormType at file offset 0): ov5 0x0214E480 (a small getter keyed on a selector struct's byte fields, used for the 'special form' dispatch path where selector+0xb's high nibble == 3) loads the SAME manager literal 0x0214BD80, the SAME field+0x40 chr_b base, and the SAME '#0x3c' stride constant via smulbb, then does a bare 'ldrb r1,[r1,r0]' (base+index, NO extra field offset added) and returns that byte -- i.e. record offset +0. This independently corroborates that the +0x40/#0x3c addressing found in claim 2 is chr_b's main array (not a coincidence of two different tables sharing a stride), and pins down record offset 0 = FormType per the known file layout.

The character run-time struct's cached index byte at +0x41 (consumed by claim 2's record-base math) is populated at spawn time in the character-init routine (arm9 0x02076E38): it copies koma-entry byte offset+6 (KomaType per docs/research/ARM9-Research-Guide.md's koma.bin layout) into new-struct+0x40, and koma-entry byte offset+7 (PassiveIndex) into new-struct+0x41, immediately followed by re-loading struct+0x40 to drive a per-character virtual-dispatch table lookup ('ldr r3,[r3,sb,lsl#2]; str r3,[r4,#8]') and re-loading it again to call another per-character dispatch whose result is stored at struct+0x42. This means the +0x41 index that claim 2's chr_b lookup uses is the koma's PassiveIndex field, not necessarily chr_b's own on-disk 'CharId' field (offset 3) -- an indexing-scheme detail worth flagging since PassiveIndex (docs say 0-55 for battle komas) and chr_b's own CharId byte values (also observed 0-55 in jus_files/exported_combat/chr_b.json) appear to share the same 0-55 numbering, but this was not independently proven equal here.
open_questions: Confirm at runtime (or by cross-checking koma.bin's actual PassiveIndex values against chr_b.json's charId column for the same roster character) whether these two 0-55 index spaces are literally identical, or merely overlapping ranges.

claims.claim: CONTRADICTS the prompt's stated ground truth. RAM address 0x0208D4A0 (arm9), given as 'chr_b identity map table', is NOT chr_b-related: its bytes are 0x00,0x01,0x02,...,0x60 (pure identity) through 0x0208D500, where the sequence jumps from 0x60 straight to 0x41 ('A') and continues 0x41,0x42,0x43... (0x0208D518 shows the matching jump back out, 0x58,0x59,0x5A,then 0x7B) -- i.e. this is a plain ASCII case-FOLDING table (lowercase a-z -> uppercase A-Z, identity elsewhere), not an index/identity map for character records. Its only two code references anywhere in the ROM (xrefs-to 0x0208D4A0 -> exactly 2 literal_loads, both at 0x02005B06/0x02005B24 inside one small arm9 function that ranges an input 0..0x7F and subtracts 0x30/0x37) belong to a text/glyph-width style routine, unrelated to chr_b, statC, or movement. Flagging this rather than silently building on it, per the task's evidence rules.
open_questions: If a distinct, genuine 'chr_b identity map' exists elsewhere (the prompt's ground truth for tier thresholds implies one was seen in an earlier round), it is not at 0x0208D4A0; suggest the original round re-locate/re-cite that address.

claims.claim: The ONLY statC consumer found (claim 2's site, arm9 0x020771C4 inside function 0x02077178) does not look like a walk-speed tier selector: it packs the [statA,statB,statC] triple onto the stack (0x020771CC-0x020771D4) and later (0x02077278-0x02077294) compares ONE of those three stack slots at a time (indexed by a 0..2 loop variable) against a 16-bit field read from a per-'move'/koma-technique data table ('ldrh r3,[r3,#2]' from a table entry, 'ldrh sl,[sl,fp]' from the stack triple) using bare EQUALITY ('cmp r3, sl; addeq ...'), incrementing a match counter only on exact equality. This is far more consistent with a koma/technique 'does this character's statA/B/C exactly satisfy this move's required stat' eligibility check (JUS's panel/koma-matching mechanic) than an inequality-based speed-tier bucket. Exhaustively cross-checking every other ldr/ldrb/ldrh/ldrsb/ldrsh with immediate offset 0xC anywhere in arm9 or any of the 14 overlays (124 total sites via search-imm) against a preceding '#0x3c'-stride record-base setup found no second occurrence -- this is the unique direct read of chr_b's raw statC field in the entire disassembled ROM.
claims.gdb_check: break 0x020771C4 (or its caller 0x0215A31C in ov5) during ordinary walking/dashing (no koma/technique menu open) and confirm whether it is ever hit purely from movement input; if it is NEVER hit outside menu/eligibility contexts, this rules the function out as the walk-speed path entirely and confirms the tier selector must read a value cached elsewhere in the character struct rather than chr_b directly.
open_questions: Where IS the cached walk-speed/tier value read from, if not chr_b's main array at runtime? Most likely candidates per the ground truth's physics offsets (+0x6A-0x7C) or timers (+0x98-0xBA) were not reachable from this round's search (see suggested_next_angles).

suggested_next_angles: THE PRIZE (Q2/Q3 tier thresholds and speed values) remains UNRESOLVED. Positive result this round: chr_b's statC is definitively at record offset +0xC in a 0x3C-byte record based at *(0x0214BD80)+0x40 (claim 2). Negative result: every one of the ~50 code sites that load the manager literal 0x0214BD80 ROM-wide was inspected, and none implement an if/else cmp-chain against statC for movement -- the sole direct statC read (claim 6) is a technique/koma stat-requirement matcher, not a speed selector. Two structural explanations were NOT yet ruled out: (a) tier selection happens ONCE at spawn/load time (inside the chr_b resource's vtable+0x2c 'GetData' virtual call itself, at 0x0207611C -- this round did not identify or disassemble the concrete vtable/class behind that virtual call, since the same generic loader code is reused for every combat .bin file and the vtable is presumably resolved by the specific resource-object type constructed for 'chr_b.bin'), caching a pre-computed speed CLASS/VALUE into the character struct rather than re-deriving it every frame; or (b) it is a direct array-index lookup (speedTable[statC] or speedTable[statC>>k]) rather than a cmp chain, which query.py's search-imm structurally cannot find (it only matches load/store IMMEDIATE offsets, not register-indexed loads or cmp/mov immediates) -- this would require manually reading disasm around statC-adjacent code for a register-offset ldrb/ldrh following a statC-sized load, not another search-imm sweep.

Q4 (dash/flash-dash speed) and Q5 (Edajima passive hook) were not reached this round due to time spent establishing Q1's addressing scheme. The most promising unexplored lead for BOTH is the per-character virtual-dispatch mechanism found incidentally in claim 4's init routine: arm9 0x02076F64-0x02076F84 does 'ldrb sb,[r4,#0x40]; ldr r3,[r3,sb,lsl#2]; str r3,[r4,#8]' (a jump/vtable-style table indexed by KomaType, cached at char_struct+8) and a second dispatch ('ldrb r3,[r4,#0x40]; ldr r2,[r2,r3,lsl#2]; blx r2; strb r0,[r4,#0x42]') whose per-character function result is cached at char_struct+0x42. Per-character behavioral hooks (like Edajima's knockback/speed exception) are far more likely to live behind one of these two dispatch tables than in a shared cmp-chain, since JUS's passive system is inherently per-character/per-koma data-driven (docs/research/ARM9-Research-Guide.md's PassiveIndex table). Tracing what the two jump-table bases (loaded from literal pools near 0x02076F5C and 0x02076F80, not yet resolved to concrete addresses this round) point to would directly answer Q5 and likely Q4 as well.

The character-context struct's own cached fields discovered this round (+0x40 = KomaType, +0x41 = PassiveIndex/koma-derived index, +0x42 = per-character dispatch result, +0x43-0x48 = per-form/koma byte table per claim 4's init routine) sit well below the ground truth's documented +0x6A-0x7C physics window and +0x78 state flag -- i.e. this is the SAME struct the other physics tracer is working on (same base 0x023D2A74 pointer chain is plausible but was not independently verified this round: `xrefs-to 0x023D2A74` and `pool-values 0x023D2A00 0x023D2B00` both returned 0 hits, meaning that exact literal never appears in any literal pool ROM-wide -- it is presumably a heap/runtime address only visible via GDB, not a static ROM constant, so cross-referencing this round's char_struct+0x40/+0x41/+0x42 offsets against a live GDB dump of that pointer chain would confirm whether the two tracers are looking at the same object.

Next concrete step for the tier thresholds specifically: identify the concrete class/vtable behind the 'GetData' virtual call at 0x0207611C for chr_b.bin specifically (distinguishing it from the identical-shaped calls used for koma.bin, jpower.bin, and the four *_collision.bin files loaded by the same routine) -- if that per-type parse function does anything beyond a raw pointer return (e.g. writes a derived array parallel to the raw 60-byte records), the tier cmp-chain or lookup table would live there, executed once at battle load rather than per-frame.
